{{Short description|Mathematical problem}}
[[File:Mixed boundary conditions.svg|right|thumb|Green: Neumann boundary condition; purple: Dirichlet boundary condition.]]
In [[mathematics]], a '''mixed boundary condition''' for a [[partial differential equation]] defines a [[boundary value problem]] in which the solution of the given equation is required to satisfy different [[boundary condition]]s on [[Disjoint sets|disjoint]] parts of the [[boundary (topology)|boundary]] of the [[domain (mathematical analysis)|domain]] where the condition is stated. Precisely, in a mixed boundary value problem, the solution is required to satisfy a [[Dirichlet boundary condition|Dirichlet]] or a [[Neumann boundary condition]] in a mutually exclusive way on disjoint parts of the boundary. 

For example, given a solution {{math|''u''}} to a partial differential equation on a domain {{math|Ω}} with boundary {{math|∂Ω}}, it is said to satisfy a mixed boundary condition if, consisting {{math|∂Ω}} of two disjoint parts, {{math|Γ{{su|b=1}}}} and {{math|Γ{{su|b=2}}}}, such that {{math|∂Ω&nbsp;<nowiki>=</nowiki>&nbsp;Γ{{su|b=1}}&nbsp;∪&nbsp;Γ{{su|b=2}}}}, {{math|''u''}} verifies the following equations:
:<math>\left. u \right|_{\Gamma_1} = u_0</math>{{spaces|10}}and{{spaces|10}}<math>\left. \frac{\partial u}{\partial n}\right|_{\Gamma_2} = g,</math>
where {{math|''u''{{su|b=0}}}} and {{math|''g''}} are given functions defined on those portions of the boundary.<ref>Obviously, it is not at all necessary to require {{math|''u''{{su|b=0}}}} and {{math|''g''}} being functions: they can be [[Distribution (mathematics)|distribution]]s or any other kind of [[generalized function]]s.</ref>

The mixed boundary condition differs from the [[Robin boundary condition]] in that the latter requires a [[linear combination]], possibly with [[pointwise]] variable coefficients, of the Dirichlet and the Neumann boundary value conditions to be satisfied on the whole boundary of a given domain.

==Historical note==
{{quote
|text= M. Wirtinger, dans une conversation privée, a attiré mon attention sur le probleme suivant: ''déterminer une fonction {{math|u}} vérifiant l'équation de Laplace dans un certain domaine'' ({{math|''D''}}) ''étant donné, sur une partie'' ({{math|''S''}}) ''de la frontière, les valeurs périphériques de la fonction demandée et, sur le reste'' ({{math|''S′''}}) ''de la frontière du domaine considéré, celles de la dérivée suivant la normale''. Je me propose de faire connaitre une solution très générale de cet intéressant problème.<ref>(English translation) "Mr. Wirtinger, during a private conversation, has drawn to my attention the following problem: ''to determine one function {{math|u}} satisfying Laplace's equation on a certain domain'' ({{math|''D''}}) ''being given, on a part'' ({{math|''S''}}) ''of its boundary, the peripheral values of the sought function and, on the remaining part'' ({{math|''S′''}}) ''of the considered domain, the ones of its derivative along the normal''. I aim to make known a very general solution of this interesting problem."</ref>
|sign= [[Stanisław Zaremba (mathematician)|Stanisław Zaremba]]
|source= {{harv|Zaremba|1910|loc=§1, p. 313}}.
}}
The first boundary value problem satisfying a mixed boundary condition was solved by [[Stanisław Zaremba (mathematician)|Stanisław Zaremba]] for the [[Laplace equation]]: according to himself, it was [[Wilhelm Wirtinger]] who suggested him to study this problem.<ref>See {{harv|Zaremba|1910|loc=§1, p. 313}}.</ref>

In the paper "''Existential analysis of the solutions of mixed boundary value problems, related to second order elliptic equation and systems of equations, selfadjoint''" (English translation of the title), Gaetano Fichera gives the first proofs of [[Existence theorem|existence]] and [[Uniqueness quantification|uniqueness theorems]] for the mixed boundary value problem involving a general second order [[Selfadjoint operator|selfadjoint]] [[elliptic operator]]s in fairly general [[Domain (mathematical analysis)|domains]].
